input.task: What is the total on this order?

provenance: M6 cold review, finding 1. `near` resolved its anchor with `page.get_by_text(near).first` — a case-insensitive SUBSTRING match, then the first result in document order. On an order summary that means the anchor 'Total' binds to **Subtotal**, and the cell beside it, $39.00, is returned as the order total with `status: success`, `verdict: PASS`, `tier: structural`, and nothing anywhere in the trace to suggest doubt.

triage.what_this_grades: the anchor half of `near`, which the whole M6 case set had left unexercised. Every other `near` case uses an anchor string that happens to occur exactly once and to be a substring of nothing longer, so all of them stay green with the anchor matched sloppily. The domain is full of the opposite: Subtotal/Total, Price/Price (incl. tax), Shipping/Shipping address, UPC/UPC code — and on Hacker News' front page every row's subline contains 'points by'.
triage.same_lesson_25_lines_up: src/browser/resolver.py already carries this exact lesson for the CANDIDATE side: `exact=True` on role names, because 'substring matching resolved absent targets to superstring siblings and extracted the wrong element as a success' (resolver-substring-name). The anchor side shipped without it.
triage.watched_red: before the fix: status success, answer $39.00 — the Subtotal.
triage.chosen_rule: prefer an exact text match when one exists, fall back to substring; among the matches keep only the deepest (get_by_text also matches ancestors of a match, which is what makes HN's nested subline work); if two matches remain that do not contain one another, the anchor is genuinely ambiguous and the run fails loudly rather than picking one.
